name: PROD: Repeat of Same Course After Completion, Same Provider — Via PUT
description: PROD baseline — companion to prod-repeat-baseline-behavior (which bundles both episodes into a single POST) and the sibling of prod-restart-baseline-behavior, but for Repeat (completion-triggered) instead of Restart (withdrawal-triggered), via PUT. A PUT represents the full current state of the learner's short courses with that provider, the same as a POST — so the repeat attempt cannot be a single-item PUT that omits the original episode; it has to be one bundled PUT carrying both: item 1 is the original episode with its completionDate now set (completing it within this same call), item 2 is the repeat attempt (new start date, same course/provider). CODE-READING: UpdateShortCourseCommandHandler.HandleSingleItem processes command.Models sequentially within one call, so item 1 is read, completed via learning.Update(), and persisted (HasActualEndDate is false going in, since the episode isn't complete yet at the start of this call) — then item 2 is read fresh from the repository, by which point the episode now has CompletionDate set and HasActualEndDate is true, so item 2 hits the short-circuit and is ignored. This depends on item 1 appearing before item 2 in the payload's onProgramme array. The assertions below confirm the short-circuit holds: 1 episode, with its StartDate and CompletionDate matching item 1 (2025-08-01 / 2026-01-15) — i.e. item 1's completion took effect and item 2 was silently ignored.

steps.name: SLD PUTs the full current state in one call: original episode completed (item 1) plus a repeat attempt (item 2)
